note: Ported from V1's subgroup_grader.py pattern: this grader always 'passes' in the surfacing sense -- a gap existing is a data fact, not itself a defect; SILENTLY DROPPING a disclosed gap is the defect. No V2 model_performance.csv equivalent exists yet (needs a real run, Stage 15); this stage tests the surfacing logic against synthetic slices.

scenarios.description: PV_MULTILINGUAL_REVIEW.md (K-023) governs multilingual case review. A terminology-normalization performance slice shows a real gap between English and German inputs -- must be surfaced, not silently averaged away.
Adversarial (the actual failure mode): the same gap as SGA-01 exists but the response's own output does not include it in a 'flagged' field -- G-MISSING_SUBGROUP_EVIDENCE fires.

Stage 21 gap-closure (INJ-072): the language-inequity inject names Arabic and Hindi specifically, not just European languages. Same surfacing rule, exercised with ar/hi slices so the grader's language-agnosticism is verified directly rather than assumed from the en/de case.
